title: var Hoisting Confusion
code:
console.log(name);
var name = 'Alice';

bugs.explanation: `var` declarations are hoisted to the top of the function scope but not their initialisation. `console.log(name)` before the assignment prints `undefined`, not the expected value. Declare with `const` or `let` and always define before use.

title: typeof null Quirk

bugs.explanation: `typeof null` returns `'object'` — a historical JavaScript quirk. Add an explicit null check before the typeof check to correctly identify objects.

title: == Coercion

bugs.explanation: `==` performs type coercion — `'5' == 5` is `true` because JS converts the string to a number. This is rarely what you intend. Use `===` for strict equality that also checks the type.

title: const Object Property Can Change
String to Number With Number()

bugs.explanation: `Number('42px')` returns `NaN` because the string contains non-numeric characters after the digits. Use `parseInt('42px', 10)` which parses as many leading digits as possible and returns `42`.

title: Ternary Operator Basics
Array Index Out of Bounds
code:
const arr = [10, 20, 30];
console.log(arr[3]);

bugs.explanation: JavaScript arrays are 0-indexed. The last element of a 3-item array is at index `2`, not `3`. Accessing `arr[3]` returns `undefined` rather than throwing — a silent bug. Use `arr[2]` or `arr[arr.length - 1]`.

title: Object Shorthand Property

bugs.explanation: When the property name matches the variable name, ES6 shorthand lets you write just `{ name, age }` instead of `{ name: name, age: age }`. This is cleaner and idiomatic modern JavaScript.

title: Template Literal vs String Concat
Falsy Values

bugs.fix: if (x !== null && x !== undefined) return true;
bugs.explanation: `if (x)` is falsy for `0`, `''`, `false`, `NaN`, `null`, and `undefined`. `hasValue(0)` returns `false` even though `0` is a valid value. Check explicitly for `null` or `undefined` if the intent is to accept any non-null value.

title: let Block Scope

bugs.explanation: `let` is block-scoped. The variable `x` only exists inside the `{}` block. Accessing it outside raises `ReferenceError`. Declare `x` outside the block if you need access to it afterwards.

title: Destructuring Array
code:
const [a, b, c] = [1, 2, 3];
console.log(a, b, c);

title: Optional Chaining
code:
const user = null;
console.log(user.name);

bugs.explanation: Accessing a property on `null` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. Use optional chaining `user?.name` which short-circuits to `undefined` when `user` is `null` or `undefined`.

title: String includes() vs indexOf()
Object.keys() Returns Strings

bugs.explanation: `Object.keys()` always returns strings, even for numeric keys. `keys[0]` is `'1'` (a string), so `keys[0] === 1` (strict) is `false`. Convert with `Number(keys[0])` before comparing to a number, or compare as strings.

title: Array spread Creates Shallow Copy
NaN Comparison

bugs.explanation: `NaN === NaN` is always `false` — NaN is the only value not equal to itself. Use `Number.isNaN(result)` to correctly detect NaN values.
